server_scripts.name: Bug Agent: Sandbox Tool: Edit File
server_scripts.script:
# Sandbox tool: edit_file, Bug Agent's own copy. The reproduce-before-fix
# discipline (reproduction_required_error) is checked here only -- Dev
# Agent, Frontend Agent and Mobile App Agent keep the shared, agent-agnostic
# "Sandbox Tool: Edit File" untouched by this gate.
# Replaces one exact, unique occurrence of old_string with new_string in an
# existing file -- for a small, targeted change where rewriting the whole
# file with write_file would be wasteful. Commits + pushes immediately on
# success, same as write_file. sandbox_dispatch is the bare HTTP primitive;
# this script owns what an edit_file call actually requires.
from one_bpmn.one_bpmn.connectors.agent_sandbox_ops import reproduction_required_error, sandbox_dispatch

target_app = (task_data.get("target_app") or "").strip()
git_branch = (task_data.get("git_branch") or "").strip()
work_item_description = (task_data.get("work_item_description") or "").strip()
path = (task_data.get("path") or "").strip()
old_string = task_data.get("old_string")
new_string = task_data.get("new_string")

if not (target_app and git_branch and work_item_description):
    result["error"] = "target_app, git_branch, and work_item_description are all required -- pass the exact same values on every call for one work order."
elif not path:
    result["error"] = "path is required, e.g. one_bpmn/one_bpmn/connectors/agent_sandbox_ops.py"
elif old_string is None or new_string is None:
    result["error"] = "old_string and new_string are both required -- old_string must appear exactly once in the file."
elif reproduction_required_error(instance, path):
    result["error"] = reproduction_required_error(instance, path)
else:
    _dispatch = sandbox_dispatch(
        "edit_file", target_app, git_branch, work_item_description,
        {"path": path, "old_string": old_string, "new_string": new_string}, context_docname, bpmn_id=bpmn_id, instance=instance,
    )
    if not _dispatch.get("ok"):
        result["error"] = _dispatch.get("error")
    else:
        result.update(_dispatch["response"])

server_scripts.name: Bug Agent: Sandbox Tool: List Files
server_scripts.script:
# Sandbox tool: list_files. Shared verbatim by every sandbox agent, so nothing here may be agent-specific.
# Lists file paths in the target app's checked-out working tree, optionally
# scoped to a prefix. sandbox_dispatch is the bare HTTP primitive; this
# script owns what a list_files call actually requires.
from one_bpmn.one_bpmn.connectors.agent_sandbox_ops import sandbox_dispatch, read_budget_exceeded

target_app = (task_data.get("target_app") or "").strip()
git_branch = (task_data.get("git_branch") or "").strip()
work_item_description = (task_data.get("work_item_description") or "").strip()
path_prefix = (task_data.get("path_prefix") or "").strip()

_budget_error = read_budget_exceeded(instance)

if not (target_app and git_branch and work_item_description):
    result["error"] = "target_app, git_branch, and work_item_description are all required -- pass the exact same values on every call for one work order."
elif _budget_error:
    result["error"] = _budget_error
else:
    _dispatch = sandbox_dispatch(
        "list_files", target_app, git_branch, work_item_description, {"path_prefix": path_prefix}, context_docname, bpmn_id=bpmn_id, instance=instance
    )
    if not _dispatch.get("ok"):
        result["error"] = _dispatch.get("error")
    else:
        result.update(_dispatch["response"])

server_scripts.name: Bug Agent: Sandbox Tool: Read File
server_scripts.script:
# Sandbox tool: read_file. Shared verbatim by every sandbox agent, so nothing here may be agent-specific.
# Reads one file's current content from the target app's checked-out
# working tree. sandbox_dispatch (agent_sandbox_ops.py) is the bare HTTP
# primitive to the sandbox -- it holds no tool policy, only what Server
# Scripts genuinely cannot do themselves (make an outbound HTTP call,
# blocked by security/script_validator.py's FORBIDDEN_MODULES). Everything
# about what a read_file call actually means -- required arguments, error
# wording -- lives here, visible and editable without a deploy.
from one_bpmn.one_bpmn.connectors.agent_sandbox_ops import sandbox_dispatch, read_budget_exceeded

target_app = (task_data.get("target_app") or "").strip()
git_branch = (task_data.get("git_branch") or "").strip()
work_item_description = (task_data.get("work_item_description") or "").strip()
path = (task_data.get("path") or "").strip()
offset = frappe.utils.cint(task_data.get("offset"))
limit = frappe.utils.cint(task_data.get("limit"))

# One spelling per file, so the repeat-read check below cannot be side-stepped.
# A model that cannot re-read a long file reaches for a path that looks new:
# "./x", "x//y", "a/../a/x", a "#L560-L700" suffix. Three Dev Agent runs on the
# BA site spent their whole 35-turn cap and $15 that way, re-fetching one 34 KB
# file a dozen times under "api/../api/..." spellings. Resolve the path to one
# canonical form first, then the dedup sees them for what they are.
_parts = []
_suffix_at = len(path)
for _mark in ("#", "?", ":"):
    if _mark in path and path.index(_mark) < _suffix_at:
        _suffix_at = path.index(_mark)
_ranged_path = _suffix_at < len(path)
_asked = path
for _part in path[:_suffix_at].split("/"):
    if not _part or _part == ".":
        continue
    if _part == "..":
        if _parts:
            _parts.pop()
        continue
    _parts.append(_part)
path = "/".join(_parts)

_budget_error = read_budget_exceeded(instance)

if not (target_app and git_branch and work_item_description):
    result["error"] = "target_app, git_branch, and work_item_description are all required -- pass the exact same values on every call for one work order."
elif not path:
    result["error"] = "path is required, e.g. one_bpmn/one_bpmn/connectors/agent_sandbox_ops.py"
elif _budget_error:
    result["error"] = _budget_error
else:
    _before = frappe.utils.now()
    _dispatch = sandbox_dispatch("read_file", target_app, git_branch, work_item_description, {"path": path}, context_docname, bpmn_id=bpmn_id, instance=instance)
    if not _dispatch.get("ok"):
        result["error"] = _dispatch.get("error")
    else:
        result.update(_dispatch["response"])
        _content = result.get("content")
        _inst = instance.name if instance else None
        if not _content:
            # Silence is what made the model guess. Name the path actually tried.
            result["error"] = (
                path + " has no content in " + target_app + " on branch " + git_branch
                + " -- either nothing exists at that path, or the file is empty. Paths are"
                + " repo-relative, e.g. one_bpmn/one_bpmn/connectors/agent_sandbox_ops.py."
                + " Use list_files to find the right one rather than trying another spelling."
            )
        else:
            _lines = _content.split("\n")
            result["path"] = path
            result["total_lines"] = len(_lines)
            if _ranged_path:
                result["note"] = (
                    "Read as " + path + ": a line range written into the path (" + _asked
                    + ") is not supported. Pass offset and limit instead."
                )
            if offset or limit:
                # A window, asked for deliberately. Never elided: the point of
                # asking for lines 600-700 is that the earlier whole-file read is
                # too big to hold, so pointing back at it would be useless.
                _from = offset if offset > 0 else 1
                if _from > len(_lines):
                    _from = len(_lines)
                _to = _from + limit - 1 if limit > 0 else len(_lines)
                if _to > len(_lines):
                    _to = len(_lines)
                if _to < _from:
                    _to = _from
                result["content"] = "\n".join(_lines[_from - 1:_to])
                result["line_range"] = str(_from) + "-" + str(_to) + " of " + str(len(_lines))
            elif _inst:
                # A repeat read of an unchanged file is the biggest waste of an
                # agent's context: whole files come back here and every result is
                # re-sent on every later turn. One Frontend run read three files
                # twice and spent 45% of its tool-result bytes on the duplicates,
                # then ran out of turns before opening its pull request. Only rows
                # from BEFORE this call count -- sandbox_dispatch writes a row for
                # this call too, and matching against that would elide the very
                # first read. Compared byte for byte rather than inferred from "we
                # did not edit it", so a file that DID change comes back in full.
                _earlier = frappe.get_all(
                    "Agent Sandbox Run",
                    filters={
                        "caller_instance": _inst,
                        "bpmn_id": bpmn_id,
                        "state": "completed",
                        "creation": ["<", _before],
                        "request_payload": ["like", '%"path": "' + path + '"%'],
                    },
                    fields=["result"],
                    order_by="creation",
                )
                _identical_before = 0
                for _row in _earlier:
                    if (frappe.parse_json(_row.result) or {}).get("content") == _content:
                        _identical_before += 1
                # Confirmed live: the note below (a successful result with a note
                # attached) was given correctly on the second read of an unchanged
                # file, and ignored -- dozens of further identical reads followed
                # it in real runs, never once reaching edit_file. A note on a
                # success is easy to skim past; an actual failed call is not. A
                # third identical read in one run is now a hard error instead.
                if _identical_before >= 2:
                    result.pop("content", None)
                    result.pop("note", None)
                    result.pop("path", None)
                    result.pop("total_lines", None)
                    result["error"] = (
                        "You have now read " + path + " three times in this run with"
                        " no change to it in between. Stop reading it: attempt the"
                        " edit with the content you already have, or ask for a"
                        " specific part with offset and limit instead of the whole"
                        " file again."
                    )
                elif _identical_before == 1:
                    result["content"] = (
                        "Unchanged since you read it earlier in this run ("
                        + str(len(_content)) + " characters, " + str(len(_lines))
                        + " lines). Do not read it again under another spelling - that"
                        + " wastes the turns you need. If you cannot still see it, ask"
                        + " for the part you need with offset and limit."
                    )
                    result["unchanged_since_earlier_read"] = True

server_scripts.name: Bug Agent: Sandbox Tool: Write File
server_scripts.script:
# Sandbox tool: write_file, Bug Agent's own copy. The reproduce-before-fix
# discipline (reproduction_required_error) is checked here only -- Dev
# Agent, Frontend Agent and Mobile App Agent keep the shared, agent-agnostic
# "Sandbox Tool: Write File" untouched by this gate.
# Writes a file's COMPLETE content into the target app's checked-out
# working tree, creating it if it does not exist, and commits + pushes the
# change immediately (see dev_agent_server.py's _commit_and_push) so the
# next tool call -- even on a different sandbox instance -- sees it.
# sandbox_dispatch is the bare HTTP primitive; this script owns what a
# write_file call actually requires.
from one_bpmn.one_bpmn.connectors.agent_sandbox_ops import reproduction_required_error, sandbox_dispatch

target_app = (task_data.get("target_app") or "").strip()
git_branch = (task_data.get("git_branch") or "").strip()
work_item_description = (task_data.get("work_item_description") or "").strip()
path = (task_data.get("path") or "").strip()
content = task_data.get("content")

if not (target_app and git_branch and work_item_description):
    result["error"] = "target_app, git_branch, and work_item_description are all required -- pass the exact same values on every call for one work order."
elif not path:
    result["error"] = "path is required, e.g. one_bpmn/one_bpmn/connectors/agent_sandbox_ops.py"
elif content is None:
    result["error"] = "content is required -- the file's full new content, not a diff."
elif reproduction_required_error(instance, path):
    result["error"] = reproduction_required_error(instance, path)
else:
    _dispatch = sandbox_dispatch(
        "write_file", target_app, git_branch, work_item_description, {"path": path, "content": content}, context_docname, bpmn_id=bpmn_id, instance=instance
    )
    if not _dispatch.get("ok"):
        result["error"] = _dispatch.get("error")
    else:
        result.update(_dispatch["response"])

server_scripts.name: Bug Programmer Write A2A Result
server_scripts.script:
# Bug Programmer — report the outcome to the A2A Task.
# `state` is written here rather than left to the reconciler: a worker map that
# writes the row directly wins, and waiting for the poller left finished
# delegations sitting at "working".
# The sandbox outcome is read off the Agent Sandbox Run rows, never off the
# model's prose: the last open_pull_request run says whether a PR exists.
_worker = frappe.db.get_value("A2A Task", context_docname, "instance")
_pr = None
_tests_passed = None
_failure = None
_files_changed = []
for _run in frappe.get_all(
    "Agent Sandbox Run",
    filters={"caller_instance": _worker},
    fields=["state", "pr_url", "error_message", "request_payload"],
    order_by="creation asc",
) if _worker else []:
    _payload = frappe.parse_json(_run.request_payload or "{}") or {}
    _action = _payload.get("action")
    if _run.pr_url:
        _pr = _run.pr_url
    if _action == "run_tests":
        _tests_passed = _run.state == "completed"
    if _run.state == "failed" and not _run.pr_url:
        _failure = _run.error_message
    if _run.state == "completed" and _action in ("edit_file", "write_file"):
        _path = (_payload.get("args") or {}).get("path")
        if _path and _path not in _files_changed:
            _files_changed.append(_path)

_text = (bug_programmer_result or "").strip()
if not _text:
    # The model's own narration came back empty -- usually a run that hit its
    # turn cap mid tool-call rather than stopping to explain. Silence here
    # used to read as "nothing happened", but real edits can (and did) still
    # land and get pushed to the branch before the cap hit. Ground the
    # fallback in what the sandbox actually recorded, not a bare placeholder,
    # so the coordinator can tell real progress from a genuinely empty run.
    if _files_changed:
        _text = (
            "The Bug Programmer did not finish with its own summary, but real "
            "changes were pushed to this branch: " + ", ".join(_files_changed) + ". "
        )
        if _tests_passed is True:
            _text += "The most recent run_tests call passed."
        elif _tests_passed is False:
            _text += "The most recent run_tests call failed -- this fix is NOT confirmed working."
        else:
            _text += "run_tests was never confirmed to pass or fail."
    else:
        _text = "The Bug Programmer finished but produced no report, and no file changes were recorded either."

if _pr and _pr not in _text:
    _text += "\n\nPull request: " + _pr
_answer = {"text": _text, "pull_request": _pr, "tests_passed": _tests_passed, "failure": _failure, "files_changed": _files_changed}
frappe.db.set_value(
    "A2A Task",
    context_docname,
    {
        "result": frappe.as_json(_answer),
        "status_message": ("Pull request opened: " + _pr) if _pr else _text[:140],
        "state": "completed",
    },
)
result["answered"] = True
result["pull_request"] = _pr
# The delegation row follows the task through task_store, and this script writes
# `state` straight to the row - so tell it here too, or the Agent Delegation a
# person reads sits at "In Progress" for work that finished.
from one_bpmn.agents.a2a import delegation
delegation.sync_from_task(frappe.get_doc("A2A Task", context_docname))

server_scripts.name: Bug Programmer: Read Instruction
server_scripts.script:
# Bug Programmer - Read the A2A Task's instruction.
# This map is started by an A2A Task insert (context_doctype="A2A Task"),
# so context_docname IS the A2A Task whose request_payload carries the
# free-text work order the delegating caller supplied — the same
# {"instruction": "..."} shape local.delegate() always builds, whether the
# caller is a real orchestrator or a standalone test insert.
if context_doctype != "A2A Task" or not context_docname:
    frappe.throw(
        "Bug Programmer: expected an A2A Task as this instance's context, got "
        + str(context_doctype) + " " + str(context_docname)
    )

payload = frappe.parse_json(doc.request_payload or "{}") or {}
instruction = (payload.get("instruction") or "").strip()

if not instruction:
    frappe.throw(
        "Bug Programmer: A2A Task " + str(context_docname)
        + " has no instruction in its request_payload to work from."
    )

work_item = (payload.get("work_item") or "").strip()
pull_request = (payload.get("pull_request") or "").strip()
target_app = (payload.get("target_app") or "").strip()
git_branch = (payload.get("git_branch") or "").strip()
# target_app and git_branch come from the Work Item's own fields via the delegation
# payload. Stated as values at the top so the model repeats them byte-for-byte on
# every sandbox call; absent when the reporter left them blank, and then the
# prompt's fallback rules apply.
_header = "Work Item: " + work_item + ("\nPull request: " + pull_request if pull_request else "") if work_item else ""
if target_app or git_branch:
    _header += ("\n" if _header else "") + "Sandbox arguments - pass these EXACT values on every sandbox tool call:"
    if target_app:
        _header += "\n  target_app: " + target_app
    if git_branch:
        _header += "\n  git_branch: " + git_branch
if _header:
    instruction = _header + "\n\n" + instruction
result["work_item"] = work_item
result["pull_request"] = pull_request
result["target_app"] = target_app
result["git_branch"] = git_branch
result["instruction"] = instruction
result["needs_tools"] = False
